note: Written for this project (MIT). Template snippets are our own.

patterns.name: Two Pointers
patterns.when: Sorted arrays, pairs/triplets with a target sum, in-place removal, palindromes.
patterns.idea: Move a left and a right index toward each other (or both forward) so each element is visited once: O(n) instead of O(n²).

patterns.name: Sliding Window
patterns.when: Longest/shortest contiguous subarray or substring that satisfies a condition.
patterns.idea: Grow the window on the right; shrink it from the left while the condition breaks. Each index enters and leaves once.

patterns.name: Fast & Slow Pointers
patterns.when: Cycles in linked lists or sequences, the middle of a list.
patterns.idea: One pointer moves 1 step, the other 2 steps. If there is a cycle they meet; when the fast one ends, the slow one is in the middle.
patterns.template:
slow = fast = head
while fast and fast.next:
    slow = slow.next
    fast = fast.next.next
    if slow is fast:
        return True
return False

patterns.name: Merge Intervals
patterns.when: Overlapping ranges: meetings, bookings, merging time slots.
patterns.idea: Sort by start time, then walk once and merge each interval into the last one if they overlap.

patterns.name: Cyclic Sort
patterns.when: Numbers in a known range 1..n (or 0..n): find missing or duplicate numbers.
patterns.idea: Put each number at the index it belongs to by swapping; the positions that are wrong afterwards are the answer.

patterns.name: In-place Linked List Reversal
patterns.when: Reverse a whole list or parts of it without extra memory.
patterns.idea: Keep prev, cur and next pointers and flip one arrow at a time.
patterns.template:
prev, cur = None, head
while cur:
    nxt = cur.next
    cur.next = prev
    prev, cur = cur, nxt
return prev

patterns.name: Tree BFS
patterns.when: Level by level work on trees: level order, right side view, minimum depth.
patterns.idea: Use a queue; process the tree one level (one queue length) at a time.

patterns.name: Tree DFS
patterns.when: Paths, depths, subtree properties, validating trees.
patterns.idea: Recursion: solve for the left and right subtree, then combine the answers at the current node.

patterns.name: Two Heaps
patterns.when: Running median, or balancing a small half and a big half of the data.
patterns.idea: A max-heap holds the smaller half and a min-heap the bigger half; keep their sizes within one.
patterns.template:
small, large = [], []  # max-heap (negated), min-heap
heappush(small, -num)
heappush(large, -heappop(small))
if len(large) > len(small):
    heappush(small, -heappop(large))

patterns.name: Subsets & Backtracking
patterns.when: All combinations, permutations, subsets, board puzzles.
patterns.idea: Build the answer step by step; at each step choose, recurse, then undo the choice.
patterns.template:
res = []
def backtrack(start, path):
    res.append(path[:])
    for i in range(start, len(nums)):
        path.append(nums[i])
        backtrack(i + 1, path)
        path.pop()
backtrack(0, [])

patterns.name: Modified Binary Search
patterns.when: Sorted or rotated arrays, or searching over an answer range ("minimum speed that works").
patterns.idea: Keep a range [lo, hi] and cut it in half each step using a condition that is monotonic.

patterns.name: Top K Elements
patterns.when: The k largest, smallest, most frequent or closest items.
patterns.idea: Keep a heap of size k; the heap root is always the current k-th best item. O(n log k).

patterns.name: K-way Merge
patterns.when: Merge several sorted lists or find the smallest item across them.
patterns.idea: Push the head of each list into a min-heap; pop the smallest and push its next item.
patterns.template:
heap = [(lst[0], i, 0) for i, lst in enumerate(lists) if lst]
heapify(heap)
while heap:
    val, i, j = heappop(heap)
    out.append(val)
    if j + 1 < len(lists[i]):
        heappush(heap, (lists[i][j + 1], i, j + 1))

patterns.name: Topological Sort
patterns.when: Tasks with dependencies, course prerequisites, build order.
patterns.idea: Count incoming edges; repeatedly take nodes with zero incoming edges (Kahn's algorithm). If some remain, there is a cycle.

patterns.name: Dynamic Programming
patterns.when: Count ways, min/max cost, yes/no questions with overlapping subproblems.
patterns.idea: Define the state (what dp[i] means), the transition from smaller states, and the base case. Cache it or fill a table.

patterns.name: Graph Traversal & Union-Find
patterns.when: Grids, islands, connected components, shortest paths in unweighted graphs.
patterns.idea: BFS/DFS visits every cell once; Union-Find merges groups and answers "are these connected?" almost in O(1).
